I've been using a smart lock on my front door for five to six years now and have tried quite a few models along the way. For most users, the ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint is a solid pick — it supports Apple Home, has built-in Wi-Fi, and offers a comprehensive set of unlocking methods. Whether you prefer fingerprint recognition or a simple PIN code, this lock can pretty much meet all your needs.

HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips, and everything related to Apple's smart home framework.

Apple Home support, but no Home Key

ULTRALOQ positions the Bolt Fingerprint as its first smart lock to fully integrate with Apple Home, and that integration is exactly what drew me to it. Honestly, I still miss Touch ID on the iPhone to this day. You can lock or unlock your door through the Home app or Siri, and if you have a HomePod or Apple TV acting as a home hub, it works just like any other Apple Home accessory — you can build it into automations and control it remotely, with full support for scenes and automation routines.

That said, there's still one missing feature for me: Home Key support. Being able to simply tap your iPhone or Apple Watch to open the door — that's what really feels like an upgrade. Even though it's missing only this one thing, it's not exactly a deal-breaker.

I hope ULTRALOQ considers adding this feature in its next model, because with Home Key, this lock could go from being "good" to being "nearly perfect." At the same time, the lock also works with Amazon Alexa, Google Home, SmartThings, and IFTTT — so no matter which smart home platform you prefer, or if you decide to switch down the road, there's plenty of flexibility. It uses 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi rather than Bluetooth, which means you can handle basic remote control through its app without needing an extra bridge.

More ways to unlock than you'll ever need

The Bolt Fingerprint offers more ways to unlock than you can count. The fingerprint reader can store up to 50 fingerprints and 50 codes, you can unlock it from your phone's app, unlock automatically as you approach the door, or use voice control through Siri, Alexa, or Google Assistant. It also comes with two physical keys, so you'll never be completely locked out even if the battery dies. For me, a smart lock without a physical key backup is completely unacceptable.

You can also customise up to 50 codes, and you can hand out one-time or time-limited codes to friends, visitors, or cleaning staff, for example. If you rent out property, this feature alone is worth the price.

There's also a "Lockout Mode" that temporarily disables all electronic unlocking methods, including codes and app access, giving people who are away for extended periods an extra layer of security to keep the home safer while it's empty. Personally, I don't see features like this as essential for a smart lock, but having them certainly doesn't hurt.

Installation and adding to Apple Home

I've installed more smart locks over the past few years than I can count, so I've got plenty of experience at this point. With the right tools, I can usually get it done in around ten minutes. Assuming you're replacing a modern deadbolt, the install involves no wiring or drilling. All you need is a Phillips screwdriver, and remember to swap out the strike plate on the door frame as well.

Once the lock is added to your Apple Home setup and assigned to a room, you can control it through the Home app or weave it into automations and scenes — triggering multiple actions at once, like having the lights come on the moment the front door is unlocked.

Wrapping up the ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint

Overall, if you don't need Home Key support, the ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint is a solid choice. Fingerprint unlock will likely end up being your most-used everyday method. Installation is also very straightforward. I've been using one on my office door for a while now, since there are often laptops sitting around waiting to be shipped out, and I wanted an extra layer of security. I really enjoy the auto-unlock feature as I approach the door, as well as being able to keep track of who's come and gone. The fingerprint unlock reminds me of the Touch ID days.

You can pick up the ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint directly from Amazon or the ULTRALOQ official website.
